key_insight: Training LLMs to explicitly perform divide‑and‑conquer (DAC) — decomposing problems into subproblems, solving them (potentially in parallel), then recombining answers — substantially improves test‑time scalability and robustness compared to strictly sequential chain‑of‑thought.
problem_solved: Chain‑of‑thought reasoning is often insufficient at the limits of model capability and inherently sequential, limiting exploration and scalability at test time; the paper addresses how to make LLM reasoning scale to larger, more complex tasks.
method: Fine‑tune or supervise LLMs to produce structured decompositions of complex problems (explicit subproblems and solving plans).
Solve subproblems independently (enabling parallelism and targeted search) and optionally iterate recursively on difficult subparts.
Aggregate and verify subanswers with a recomposition step and use training signals that reward useful decompositions and correct final solutions.
impact: This approach lets practitioners scale reasoning to bigger tasks by exploiting parallelism and better exploration, improving reliability of LLMs on problems that exceed single‑chain capacity.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input problem → decomposition tree → parallel subproblem solvers → recomposition → final answer.
Comparison chart: CoT (sequential) vs DAC (parallel/recursive) showing test‑time runtime/accuracy tradeoffs as problem size grows.
Example decomposition tree: a concrete problem split into subquestions with solved leaves and merged result.
Icon set: magnifying glass (analysis), branching tree (decomposition), gears/parallel nodes (concurrent solving), checkmark (recomposition/verification).
paper_title: Training LLMs for Divide-and-Conquer Reasoning Elevates Test-Time Scalability
paper_authors: Xiao Liang, Zhong-Zhi Li, Zhenghao Lin, Eric Hancheng Jiang, Hengyuan Zhang
